D.why: Pale ash skirt with a real side bell and a tall spiked crown reads most like a gown from above.
D.fix: Slim the full-width grey sleeves and add a glowing violet hem seam and waist gem.

F.why: Charred black bodice over a pale lilac skirt with a violet waist gem is the clearest dress read.
F.fix: Slim the bulky black sleeves, widen the hem, and replace the yellow headband with a bone or violet crown.

B.why: The violet flame-crown is the most epic, light-ready idea, but block sleeves and a near-straight skirt read armoured.
B.fix: Slim the sleeves, bell out the skirt, and open the black box hood under the crown.

E.why: Bone crown and rib skirt are zone-true and distinctive, but the straight ribs read as a cage, not a flare.
E.fix: Fan the bone ribs outward from the hip into a bell with fewer, bolder panels.

A.why: Flat mortarboard hat and stacked equal-width slabs read as a pagoda or armour, all mid-grey.
A.fix: Replace the flat cap with a tall slim circlet and make the tiers widen strongly toward the hem.

C.why: All-black boxy figure with huge sleeves vanishes into the night and has almost no violet light.
C.fix: Bring ash grey and bone white into the bodice and add a glowing violet hem and crown.

notes: No candidate solved the wave's headline ask: every set still has full shoulder-width block sleeves. D and F lead on gown read (light skirt, defined waist); B has the best epic crown and E the best zone-true bone motif, and a merge of D's bell, F's contrast and B or E's crown would be strongest. Violet Neon is underused across the board; most sets need a glowing hem seam plus one waist gem.
